correctness.rationale: Exact parameterization gives (1). For p>=0 both pointwise factors grow strictly. For -1<p<0 the differentiated energy splits into a negative term N and positive T. T=O(a log(1/a)), while rescaling t=az and a uniform integrable majorant yield N/a^p -> 2p sqrt(pi) Gamma((1-p)/2)/Gamma(1-p/2)<0. Integrating from the finite needle limit proves the exact nonzero a^(p+1) coefficient and its sign. At a=1 the derivative is pi(p+1)>0, so an interior minimizer exists. A diagonal map and the tip support direction give Hausdorff distance a/2 between K_a and K_{a/2}; difference of asymptotics yields the claimed positive quotient. The numerical quadrature checker independently passed for p=-.9,-.5,-.1 and p=0,1,2. No conclusion is based on finite sampling alone.

evidence: Saracco--Stefani (arxiv:2306.07770v1) characterize weights inclusion-monotone for *every* nested convex pair without imposing the origin; their counterexamples are not constrained to concentric ellipses.
Csató--Giovagnoli (arxiv:2610.11677v1) prove positive-p monotonicity and construct different negative-weight failures; neither conclusion supplies the full smooth nested-ellipse phase transition.

Csató--Giovagnoli--Roy (arxiv:2608.19851v1) prove E_p(K)<=4^{-p} P(K)^{p+1}/(p+1) for -1<p<0 among symmetric plane curves (with matching normalization), which bounds the ellipse using its changing perimeter P(K_a)>4 but does not compare it with F_p(0+)=4/(p+1).

originality.rationale: A complete comparison of the closest available primary works and a published weighted-perimeter Hölder theorem revealed the known positive-power inclusion theorem, an older unrestricted-family rigidity statement, sharp global exponent p+1 via disk scaling, and a symmetric fixed-perimeter needle inequality. None of these results states or mathematically implies the negative signed cusp constant for fixed-major-axis thin ellipses, the exact all-exponent inclusion threshold within that smooth nested family, or its interior minimizer. The sources are credited; global novelty is not certified.
residual_risks: The complete historical literature, particularly older ellipse-moment integral tables or unindexed singular perturbation arguments, is not exhausted; mathematical priority remains provisional.
A published global Hölder exponent is stronger in one respect (all convex sets); this work claims only the new signed ellipse cusp and restricted monotonicity phase behavior.

Primary MSC 52A40 matches the published geometric Hausdorff-modulus result directly refined here. The underlying analytic papers have primary MSC 49Q10 and are cited as supporting literature rather than as the slot-owning source.

value.rationale: The motivating 2026 convex-geometric monotonicity theorem imposes a nondecreasing-weight condition; this result establishes a sharp exponent-wise necessity even on the maximally natural restricted class of smooth nested, origin-centered ellipses. The signed gamma cusp and exact fixed-axis Hausdorff scaling quantify why negative powers reverse the inequality; an interior minimizer follows for every negative admissible exponent. This is more than a single numerical example, and it distinguishes an already-known general Hölder exponent from a new geometric shape-specific sharp coefficient and sign.
